To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) catastrophic interference is a major problem for multiple sequence learning, (2) catastrophic interference can be prevented in multiple sequence learning by using pseudopattern sequences, (3) the pseudopattern sequences are generated by reverberating Elman networks, and (4) the pseudopatter ns are coupled to the input of the main Elman network.
the architecture of the coupled reverberating Elman network (CREN) allows it to learn multiple sequences of patterns without catastrophic interference.
the use of a reverberating Elman network with a pseudopattern input layer can prevent the catastrophic interference problem in multiple sequence learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning and storing multiple sequences.
the problem of catastrophic interference in multiple sequence learning using a coupled reverberating Elman architecture.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Elman network is a good model of human language learning and that it has a number of advantages over other models.

the Elman network, as a recurrent network, is able to model the human learning process in a better way than a static feed-forward network, but the Elman network has its own problems, such as the catastrophic interference problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the Elman network can be used as a model for a cognitive agent, but only if we modify it in two important ways.

we have shown that it is possible for a connectionist system to learn multiple sequences of patterns without catastrophic interference using pseudopattern sequences, and that it does so in a way that allows the network to generalize from one sequence to the other.
the pseudopatterns are generated by the recurrent connections between the input and output nodes of the Elman network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pseudopatterns that we use to learn the sequences are not the same as the patterns that are used to recognize the sequences.
it is possible to learn multiple sequences in a single network without catastrophic interference.
the architecture we have developed, the Coupled Reverberation Elman Network (CREN), can learn multiple sequential tasks without catastrophic interference.
